subject.title: fix(telegram): Allow multi-agent ACP bindings within same account

question: Should same-account Telegram ACP binds in the same group topic become truly independent simultaneous bindings, or should OpenClaw only allow an explicit same-account handoff where the newest binding owns the topic?
rationale: The PR description asks for independent multi-agent bindings, but both current and PR storage/routing resolve one record per account/topic, so choosing independent bindings versus handoff affects the session-state and inbound-routing contract.

options.title: Require Independent Bindings
options.body: Rework the current plugin-state manager and routing model so multiple same-account session keys can coexist in one topic with explicit selection semantics.

options.title: Accept Same-Account Handoff
options.body: Narrow the PR to a deliberate last-writer-wins ownership switch and update tests, wording, and proof to stop claiming independent bindings.

options.title: Keep Single-Owner Topics
options.body: Reject same-topic multi-agent binding until maintainers design a broader routing model for multiple active ACP sessions in one topic.

recommendation.title: Require Independent Bindings
recommendation.body: Rework the current plugin-state manager and routing model so multiple same-account session keys can coexist in one topic with explicit selection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current plugin-state binding storage and ACP persistence history point to this person as the strongest routing candidate for the binding-model decision.
